clue.text: Pay out place money

parts.note: to spot something is to place or locate it
cash is ready money

explanation.surface: Settling up the winnings on a horse that came in second or third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place money' sounds like a racing bet on a horse finishing placed, but it splits into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot cash is payment made immediately on delivery, a payout handed over on the spot.

clue.text: It uses different trains

indicators.note: made different, so the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Something that runs on a variety of railway services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' looks like railway carriages; here it means retinues, the followers of a dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite is a body of attendants following a great person, as a train is.

clue.text: Predator that swoops down and circles over its quarry

definitions.text: Predator that swoops down and circles over its quarry

parts.words: Predator that swoops down and circles over its quarry
parts.note: a description of a fish-eating hawk hunting over water

explanation.surface: A bird of prey hunting its victim from above.
explanation.definitionFit: This large raptor hovers over water and plunges feet first to seize fish.

clue.text: Versatile actors who speak a Slav tongue

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a plural noun, people speaking it

indicators.note: versatile performers can turn into other forms, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Adaptable performers who can manage a Slavonic language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Versatile' seems to describe the actors' talent but signals that their letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatian is a South Slavonic language, spoken by the people of Croatia.

clue.text: As fast as one can go along the highway

definitions.text: As fast as one can go along the highway

parts.words: As fast as one can go along the highway
parts.note: read as the top legal speed allowed on a road, not one's flat-out pace

explanation.surface: A driver racing down the road at full throttle.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal maximum velocity on a road is the fastest one may lawfully travel.

clue.text: Burn to break 4,perhaps

explanation.surface: Driving so fast that you burn rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 refers to the answer at 4 down, SPEED-LIMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to sear with heat, and also old slang for driving at reckless speed, beyond the legal maximum.

clue.text: An agreement to cut down the work force, maybe

definitions.text: cut down the work force, maybe

explanation.surface: A deal made to reduce the staff numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work force' suggests employees; it can equally be the muscle force that shortens when muscles tighten.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal bargain between parties, and a verb meaning to shrink or reduce in size.

clue.text: A prospect one doesn't look forward to

definitions.text: A prospect one doesn't look forward to

parts.words: A prospect one doesn't look forward to
parts.note: a prospect is a view; this one is seen looking backwards, as in a car mirror

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant ahead that one dreads.
explanation.definitionFit: The view behind a vehicle, seen in its mirror, faces the opposite way to travel.

clue.text: Don is in the soup he thinks of nothing but pleasure!

definitions.text: he thinks of nothing but pleasure

indicators.note: the words Don is sit inside the stirred letters
soup is a mixture, so the letters of the word before are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A university don in trouble who cares only for enjoying himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' turns THE into HET, and 'in' puts DONIS inside it. 'In the soup' looks like the idiom for being in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to pleasure as life's chief good is a pleasure-seeker in the classical philosophical sense.

clue.text: I'm put to the test and made better

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
to prove something is to test it, as in proving ground

explanation.surface: Someone saying they have been tested and come out improved.
explanation.definitionFit: Improved means enhanced or bettered.

clue.text: What the world's most underdeveloped countries want retracted?

parts.note: the United Nations represents the world, so the world's gives UN's
what poor nations seek is aid

explanation.surface: Asking what the poorest nations of the world would like taken back.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as UN's aid; the apostrophe in 'world's' supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that are retracted are taken back, as if never spoken.

clue.text: Balanced flow of currency that comes rather late in the day

definitions.text: that comes rather late in the day
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun, a time of day

parts.note: even means level or balanced
a current is a flow, and a tide is a flow of the sea's current

explanation.surface: A steady stream of money that turns up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' looks like money but means a flowing current, as of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: Fearful sort of cavern

indicators.note: sort is read as a verb, to sort or rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: A frightening kind of cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Craven means cowardly, lacking courage.

clue.text: Things that come in handy for keeping cuttings?

definitions.text: Things that come in handy for keeping cuttings?

parts.words: Things that come in handy for keeping cuttings?
parts.note: cuttings read as press cuttings fastened together, not plant cuttings in a garden

explanation.surface: Useful garden aids for propagating plant cuttings.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bent wire fasteners hold sheets of paper, such as newspaper clippings, together.

clue.text: Moneyed men who move around in fine cars

indicators.note: the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Rich people driving about in expensive cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move around' rearranges IN with FINE CARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Financiers are capitalists who deal in large sums of money.

clue.text: The Hooter at the milk depot, possibly

definitions.text: The Hooter at the milk depot, possibly

parts.words: The Hooter at the milk depot, possibly
parts.note: a hooting bird pictured at a dairy among its milk vessels

explanation.surface: The factory siren at a dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: A churn is a large milk can and an owl is a hooter; the whole is an old name for the nightjar, a bird with a churring call.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect name for the nightjar, a nocturnal bird with a whirring song.

clue.text: Can I last out as a classical scholar? yes

indicators.note: the word last is spread outside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one can stay the course as a scholar of the ancients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last out' reads as endure, but LAST goes around TIN and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latinist is an expert in the Latin language and literature.

clue.text: Old socialist reformers who now support the Alliance

explanation.surface: Political followers then and now.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alliance was the 1980s British partnership of the Liberals and the SDP, which David Owen led; Robert Owen was a 19th-century socialist reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Robert Owen's co-operative socialism, and supporters of David Owen of the Social Democrats.

clue.text: The first chap in the queue for a senior hotel appointment

definitions.text: The first chap in the queue

explanation.surface: Lining up early to apply for a top hotel job.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first sense as the one waiting at the head of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who waits at the front of a line, and the chief of the dining-room staff.

clue.text: Italian city that can make one mad…

indicators.note: the letters can be made into something else by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A city in Italy that drives a visitor crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Modena is a city in Emilia-Romagna, northern Italy.

clue.text: … whenever one chooses a woven fabric

explanation.surface: Picking any cloth one likes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as A TWILL, a twill being cloth with diagonal ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: As one pleases, at one's pleasure; and an article plus a diagonally ribbed cloth.

clue.text: Puts pressure on the men who sail in a ship?

definitions.text: the men who sail in a ship?

explanation.surface: Squeezing a ship's company.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as S CREWS: a ship's crews.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce or squeeze someone; and the sailors who man a vessel.

clue.text: Gives a ruling about doctored gins

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: doctored drink is tampered with, so these letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A verdict delivered on spiked spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives a ruling' looks like a judge's verdict but means rules as a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign who reigns rules over a realm.

clue.text: A piece of verse that's initially puzzling

definitions.text: A piece of verse that's initially puzzling

parts.words: A piece of verse that's initially puzzling
parts.note: a poem whose line openings spell out a hidden message, a puzzle in its first letters

explanation.surface: A poem that baffles at first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem in which the first letters of the lines spell a word or name.

clue.text: A poet I arrange to soothe medically

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet putting together something to calm a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To opiate is to dull or calm with a narcotic drug.

clue.text: A shockingly energetic fellow!

parts.note: shockingly suggests an electric charge carried by a cable that is switched on

explanation.surface: An outrageously lively man.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively, energetic person is likened to a cable carrying current.

clue.text: Most up-to date feature of a desolate stretch of land

indicators.note: the answer is a feature found within these words

explanation.surface: The newest thing about a barren piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest thing is the newest or most recent.

clue.text: Reappraisal of USA's last storms

indicators.note: a reappraisal looks again and reorders, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive S is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: A review of America's most recent bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storms' looks like weather but is a verb: attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to attack it violently.
